newsitem.title: UK: Thames, utility stocks up after FT comment.
newsitem.headline: Thames, utility stocks up after FT comment.

text.p: Shares in UK water and electricity companies rose on Wednesday after upbeat comment on utilities in the influential Financial Times Lex column.

Among water stocks, Thames Water Plc was up 11-1/2p at 636-1/2 by 0822 GMT, Severn Trent Water Plc was up 14p at 703-1/2, Anglian Water Plc was up 9p at 614 and United Utilities Plc was up 11-1/2p at 675.
Among electricity stocks, National Power Plc was up 4p at 505-1/2, PowerGen Plc was up 5-1/2p at 622 and Yorkshire Electricity Plc was up 5-1/2p at 839.

The FT said a victory in the election -- due by the end of May -- by the opposition Labour Party, which has promised a windfall tax on utility profits, had been overdiscounted by water and electricity companies.
It said it was in Labour's interest to overstate the size of the possible tax.
"Even a Labour victory offers the potential for substantial outperformance as uncertainty clears," it said, pointing out that water companies in particular offer scope for further cost-cutting.
The water sector "has not unlocked its cash riches as electricity companies have, but Scottish Power is busy showing Southern Water just how much fat-cutting water companies have to do," the FT said.
